summary: Christopher S. George worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University in 1965 under Royal W. Weiler, as well as under Padma Gyaltsen and Geshe Wangyal. He was a professor at the IASWR (~1974–1985).
Chu-tsing Li was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Iowa (~1949–1955) and held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1966 to 1990.

Chuan-ying Yen is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Harvard University (~1980–1986) under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield and teacher John Hay, and was tutored by Chu-tsing Li.

Chun-fang Yu works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1966–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001–2013).

Chun-min Yen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of Arizona (~1998–2004) under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello and teacher Todd Brown, also studying under traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Oxford (1963) and St Antony's College (~1963–1967) after studying under Khenpo Gangshar, Jamgon Kongtrul, Dilgo Khyentse, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Shechen Kongtrul.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo.
Clare Carlisle works in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1995–2002) and served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011).

Claude Jacques specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under George Cœdès (~1958–1968), taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973–1998), and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1989–1993).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn in 1999.

Claudia Wenzel specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Alexander L. Mayer and completed her studies under doctoral supervisor Lothar Ledderose (~1995–2000).

Claudius Buchanan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (1782) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College.

Claus Oetke was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1982). He served as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent at the University of Hamburg (~1983–1989) and later held a post at Stockholm University (~1989–2014).

Claus Vogel was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1964–1976), the University of Göttingen (~1976–1977), and the University of Bonn as Prof. Dr. in 1976.

Clifford Geertz was a scholar in religious studies who studied at Antioch University (~1946–1950) and Harvard (~1950–1956). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1960–1970), Princeton University (~1970–2000), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1970–2000).

Colette Caillat was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Louis Renou (~1945–1965). She served as Director at the University of Paris (~1967–1989) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1979–2007).

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University (~2006–2010) under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at Deakin University under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at Dollar Academy. He served as the Surveyor-General of India at the Survey of India from circa 1815 to 1821.

Collett Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a PhD at Columbia (~1976–1983) under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku Universities. She became a professor at the University of Washington (1996).
